nodes.rationale: Deleting a tag cleanly drops its assignments everywhere; deleting a tagged object removes just the assignments — the tag survives.

nodes.label: Racks REST API (GET /api/v1/racks)
nodes.rationale: Every page facet is a query param (q, site_id, group_id, ungrouped, room, height_u, occupancy, min_free_u, max_free_u); CSV sets (height_u=42,24) with AND semantics, 422 on bad values.

nodes.label: First-run setup (/setup, IPAMBOX_PASSWORD[_FILE])
nodes.rationale: Prefer IPAMBOX_PASSWORD_FILE (e.g. a Docker secret) so the password never sits in env/compose files.

nodes.label: Sessions & brute-force protection
nodes.rationale: Two independent protections: 5-strike lockout per (user, IP) pair plus a per-IP credential-stuffing backstop that ignores username.

nodes.label: Users & Roles console + Account & Security
nodes.rationale: Changing a user's role or password revokes all of their sessions immediately.

nodes.label: Certificate fields (platform, target, server name, expires_on, serial)
nodes.norm_label: certificate fields (platform, target, server name, expires_on, serial)

nodes.label: Changelog coverage & retention
nodes.rationale: Bulk operations write one entry per affected row — a 50-address bulk delete produces 50 traceable entries, not one opaque event.

nodes.label: Per-object history (row history button, IP drawer)
nodes.norm_label: per-object history (row history button, ip drawer)

nodes.label: Circuit import provenance (import_batch_id)
nodes.rationale: The circuits sheet doubles as a site directory (site name → site number + prefix mapping), so it's a good first sheet to import.

nodes.label: Confirm/delete workflow
nodes.rationale: Confirm promotes a discovered host into a normal active address; delete rejects it and the changelog records the decision.

nodes.label: MAC mismatch review (mac_was vs mac_seen)
nodes.rationale: A MAC mismatch usually means a NIC swap or a spoof; the live value wins but the row stays flagged until reviewed.

nodes.label: Going quiet — active↔offline flips
nodes.rationale: Only genuinely new things require a human decision; silent hosts flip to offline and back automatically.

nodes.label: Roll-up utilization (agg_used_ips, allocated_pct, descendant_count)
nodes.rationale: A container that's 100% allocated but 40% used is fully assigned yet still half empty — the tree surfaces that difference at a glance.

nodes.label: API docs — Swagger at http://<host>:8001/docs
nodes.rationale: User guide vs machine-readable API reference: same path, different port; open it directly for scripting.

nodes.label: UI tour — sidebar groups and header
nodes.norm_label: ui tour — sidebar groups and header
nodes.rationale: Sidebar grouped like the data: Dashboard, IPAM, Inventory, Operations, System.

nodes.label: Five-stage scan pipeline (ARP→ICMP→TCP→PTR→OUI)
nodes.rationale: Each stage catches hosts the previous missed: ARP for L2, ICMP ping-socket, TCP probes on configured ports, PTR reverse-DNS, then IEEE OUI vendor resolution. Persists open_ports and best-effort device_type per host.

nodes.label: Running scans (Quick scan, scans page, SSE stream, cancel)
nodes.norm_label: running scans (quick scan, scans page, sse stream, cancel)
nodes.rationale: Status lifecycle queued→running→completed/failed/cancelled with live SSE deltas, ETA and per-CIDR rate limit.

nodes.label: Runtime-tunable scanner settings (Settings→Scanning)
nodes.rationale: Changes persist in app_settings, fall back to .env defaults and reach the worker within a minute — no restart needed.

nodes.label: Go-to chords (g d/g p/g s/g i/g c/g h)
nodes.norm_label: go-to chords (g d/g p/g s/g i/g c/g h)

nodes.label: Shortcut scope rules
nodes.rationale: Single-key shortcuts never fire while typing or with a dialog open so j, k, / and ? stay safe as text; ⌘K is the exception and toggles from anywhere.

nodes.label: Table & subnet-grid keyboard navigation
nodes.rationale: j/k move rows, Alt+arrows reorder orderable lists; inside the subnet matrix arrows move between addresses and drag selects a span.

nodes.label: Site fields (slug, code, site number, active flag)
nodes.norm_label: site fields (slug, code, site number, active flag)
nodes.rationale: Code and site number drive workbook-import sheet→site matching; inactive sites are kept for history but excluded from import matching.

nodes.label: Attaching tags (row picker, edit dialog, bulk)
nodes.norm_label: attaching tags (row picker, edit dialog, bulk)
nodes.rationale: Tag chips render on rows everywhere the object appears — lists, drawers, search results.

nodes.label: VLANs — VLAN groups + VLANs
nodes.rationale: Two levels: groups bundle related VLANs, VLANs carry the actual VID; prefixes link to a VLAN so the subnet list shows the L2 domain.

nodes.label: VLAN usage tips
nodes.rationale: Keep a group per site if the same VID is reused with different meaning at different locations; VLAN→prefix linking is done from the prefix dialog.

nodes.label: VRF overlap rules in practice
nodes.rationale: Overlapping CIDRs allowed across VRFs but rejected within one by a PostgreSQL exclusion constraint; scans that don't name a VRF get one inferred when an exact-match prefix lives in exactly one VRF.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/interfaces/match-free-text
nodes.rationale: One-shot matcher linking legacy switch_name/switch_port text to real interfaces; multiple candidates reported ambiguous (never guessed), every link lands in the changelog.

nodes.label: Demo .Rackula.zip racks
nodes.rationale: demo-rack.Rackula.zip (18 devices) and demo-rack-dc.Rackula.zip (V4-era 36-device rack); device types use image-library slugs so real product images render on the elevation.

nodes.label: Cable
nodes.rationale: Joins exactly two interfaces with one-cable-per-interface enforcement; carries kind, color/label, length_m; labels searchable to both ends' devices.

nodes.label: connected_interface structured link
nodes.rationale: IP drawer's far-end port link, living alongside legacy switch_name/switch_port free text which stays as the import record and fallback.

nodes.label: Interface
nodes.rationale: Device-owned ports (rj45/sfp/qsfp/console/patch/power/other) with speed/MAC; cabled ports show their peer.

nodes.label: L1 trace
nodes.rationale: Ordered hop walk through cabled interfaces that continues through panel front↔back pairs (pass-through, not a cable); mid-chain launches surface the whole path; loops terminate at 10 hops.

nodes.label: Bulk port generation
nodes.rationale: Generate creates a whole port set in one call; pair_prefix creates same-indexed back ports and links each front↔back pair — a 24-port patch panel in one click.

nodes.label: Device inventory
nodes.rationale: First-class devices own many IPs (mgmt/service/iLO), link an asset and a site, optionally sit in a rack; health is the worst status across linked IPs; unracked devices are valid inventory.

nodes.label: Rack elevations & rack groups
nodes.rationale: Per-U placement on front/rear faces with collision validation, live scan-health dots, bayed-row groups with capacity rollups, smart-bundle CSV/XLSX round-trips.

nodes.label: Cable validation (documented vs observed)
nodes.rationale: Flags, never fixes: a mismatch never deletes or rewrites the cable — the human confirms what is true. Absent evidence is not a violation, so a failed bridge/LLDP walk can neither raise nor clear a flag; flags self-heal on the next contradictory-free poll.

nodes.label: SNMP poll pipeline (sysName → IF-MIB → bridge-MAC → LLDP)
nodes.norm_label: snmp poll pipeline (sysname → if-mib → bridge-mac → lldp)

nodes.label: Cabling, interfaces & L1 trace
nodes.rationale: Interfaces with one-cable-per-interface enforcement and an end-to-end L1 trace that hops patch-panel pass-throughs.

nodes.label: Rackula (external rack editor)
nodes.rationale: External rack-elevation editor; round-trips via share URLs and .Rackula.zip archives for heavy editing.

nodes.label: Review center (/review)
nodes.rationale: Dismissal is data, not deletion — review_dismissals rows pin a finding's fingerprint so it survives re-flagging, carries actor+note, and restores with one click.

nodes.label: Patch panel as kind=patch device
nodes.rationale: No special panel entity: a patch panel is just a device whose interfaces have kind patch, each front port paired to a same-indexed back port on the same device.

nodes.label: compose service: api (FastAPI/uvicorn, alembic upgrade head on start)
nodes.norm_label: compose service: api (fastapi/uvicorn, alembic upgrade head on start)

nodes.label: compose service: scanner (ARQ worker, host networking, NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW)
nodes.norm_label: compose service: scanner (arq worker, host networking, net_admin/net_raw)

nodes.label: ipam bridge network (192.0.2.0/24)
nodes.rationale: 192.0.2.0/24 is RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 — reserved for documentation so it can never collide with a real LAN; it pins web's 192.0.2.10 so the API trusts X-Forwarded-For from exactly that one peer.

nodes.label: Scan targeting policy (scan_networks, excludes, only_configured, max_hosts)
nodes.norm_label: scan targeting policy (scan_networks, excludes, only_configured, max_hosts)
nodes.rationale: Exclusions are enforced identically by the API route, the scheduler and the worker — a job that slips through one layer is stopped by the next.

nodes.label: Hybrid .env → DB override model
nodes.rationale: .env provides deployment defaults; UI saves write app_settings rows that take effect without a restart (worker sees scanner changes within a minute); each field shows its source (db/env/default) and can reset to the env value.

nodes.label: SNMP device credential
nodes.rationale: Credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted under the server master key and write-only — enabling SNMP without a stored credential is rejected because a poll that can't authenticate just burns timeouts.

nodes.label: Write-Only Encrypted SNMP Credentials (v1/v2c/v3)
nodes.rationale: AES-256-GCM under the server master key; write-only so credentials never appear in API responses, logs, or error messages. Enabling without a credential is rejected to avoid polls that only burn timeouts.

nodes.label: api service (FastAPI/uvicorn backend)
nodes.rationale: The API port is published on ALL interfaces by default (API_BIND=0.0.0.0) — direct /docs, /metrics and script access from the LAN is a deliberate feature; IPAMBOX_COOKIE_SECURE defaults false so logins work over plain HTTP on a LAN because browsers reject Secure cookies on non-localhost http origins.

nodes.label: ipam bridge network (192.0.2.0/24)
nodes.rationale: Subnet pinned to 192.0.2.0/24, RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 (reserved for documentation), so it can never collide with a real LAN/WAN client; changing it requires updating IPAMBOX_TRUSTED_PROXIES and web's ipv4_address together.

nodes.label: scanner service (arq worker, host networking)
nodes.rationale: Uses network_mode: host with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW so the worker gets real L2 access for ARP scanning; it reaches Postgres/Redis via the loopback-published ports of db and redis.

nodes.label: web service (Next.js frontend)
nodes.rationale: Pinned to 192.0.2.10 on the ipam bridge so IPAMBOX_TRUSTED_PROXIES on the api can trust X-Forwarded-For from exactly that one peer — nothing else on the bridge can spoof it.

nodes.label: Session-cookie authentication
nodes.rationale: Cookie sessions expire after IPAMBOX_SESSION_HOURS (default 168); brute-force protection via 5-strike lockout per (user, IP) plus a per-IP credential-stuffing backstop independent of username.

nodes.label: Address roles (vip/vrrp/hsrp/glbp/carp/secondary)
nodes.rationale: Mark addresses that float between devices so reconciliation does not treat them as ordinary hosts.

nodes.label: Address CSV import/export
nodes.rationale: Export is UTF-8-BOM CSV honoring active filters; import is all-or-nothing with a per-row error report.

nodes.label: IP drawer
nodes.rationale: Slide-out detail panel showing every field, tag chips, NAT partner, and the object's own changelog history.

nodes.label: Per-object history
nodes.rationale: The same changelog data scoped to one object via the History row action or the IP drawer.

nodes.label: ip column type (live IPAM resolution)
nodes.rationale: Resolves cells live against ip_addresses (status dot, last-seen, click opens the address drawer); unresolved IPs render muted/dashed specifically to surface drift between the list and the IPAM.

nodes.label: Site → VRF → Prefix → IP address data model
nodes.norm_label: site → vrf → prefix → ip address data model
nodes.rationale: Everything hangs off one hierarchy; overlapping CIDRs are allowed across VRFs but rejected within one; container prefixes hold children and are exempt from overlap checks.

nodes.label: Scapy scanner container
nodes.rationale: Runs Scapy with raw sockets — requires network_mode: host and NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW capabilities, Linux only; uses a bundled 58k-entry IEEE OUI database.

nodes.label: Keyboard shortcuts
nodes.rationale: Single-key shortcuts never fire while typing in a field or while a dialog/menu is open; ⌘K/Ctrl+K is the exception — it toggles the palette from anywhere.

nodes.label: container prefix
nodes.rationale: Holds child subnets and is exempt from overlap checks, so a /16 container can hold child /24s; moving a container takes its children along.

nodes.label: VLAN groups
nodes.rationale: Bundle related VLANs — keep a group per site when the same VID is reused with different meaning at different locations.

nodes.label: Global VRF
nodes.rationale: Seeded by the initial migration so a fresh install always has somewhere to put prefixes.

nodes.label: Accounts & Roles
nodes.rationale: Session-cookie login with RBAC enforced on every API route; the UI only hides what you cannot do — the backend is the authority.

nodes.label: The four roles (Administrator/Operator/Contributor/Viewer)
nodes.rationale: Guardrails: the last administrator can't demote or delete themselves, and nobody can delete their own account.

nodes.label: IP Addresses
nodes.rationale: Addresses live inside a prefix and carry both documented intent and observed reality.

nodes.label: mac_mismatch flag
nodes.rationale: A scan saw a different MAC than documented; the live value wins but the address is flagged for review and counted on the dashboard.

nodes.label: Certificates
nodes.rationale: Track certificate expiry across the estate so nothing silently lapses.

nodes.label: Changelog
nodes.rationale: Every create, update, and delete is recorded with actor, timestamp, and field-level before/after diffs — nothing changes silently; bulk ops write one entry per affected row.

nodes.label: Circuits (WAN circuit register)
nodes.rationale: One row per provider line linked to a site; is_retired keeps history without deleting.

nodes.label: Discovery Inbox
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation queue — scan findings (new hosts, MAC mismatches) land here for a human decision instead of silently mutating documented data.

nodes.label: Hierarchy Tree
nodes.rationale: Renders the whole IPAM as an expandable Site → VRF → Prefix → child Prefix tree — the fastest way to see where a subnet lives and how full each branch is.

nodes.label: Custom Lists (user-defined tables)
nodes.rationale: Exist for sheet-shaped data that does not fit a fixed entity (server rosters, contact lists, environment matrices) — anything that used to live in a workbook sheet and lose its shape on import.

nodes.label: IpamBox
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted IPAM with a built-in LAN scanner: you model the address space, the scanner verifies it, and drift shows up as data instead of surprises.

nodes.label: Row Colors
nodes.rationale: Two ways to tint list rows — manual per-row colors set by anyone who can write data, and admin-managed rule-based colors computed server-side.

nodes.label: Scans
nodes.rationale: Scanner container reconciles what it finds against documentation; scans run ad-hoc (quick scan / scans page) or on a schedule.

nodes.label: Command palette
nodes.rationale: Keyboard-first search across the whole IPAM; pasting a bare IP offers a Jump result landing on the owning prefix with the address highlighted; respects Hebrew final-letter folding.

nodes.label: Services (service catalog)
nodes.rationale: Tracks what the network serves, not just what it is made of — linking services to sites gives the blast radius when a subnet changes or a scan finds drift.

nodes.label: Backup & Restore settings section
nodes.rationale: .json.gz snapshots cover every data table; restores are atomic, preserve IDs, work on a fresh install and keep you logged in; user accounts are excluded by default with an admin opt-in for non-admin accounts.

nodes.label: Settings
nodes.rationale: Sidebar of sections mirroring deployment concerns; sections you lack permission for are hidden.

nodes.label: Sites
nodes.rationale: Top of the IpamBox hierarchy — physical or logical locations that VRFs, VLANs, prefixes, circuits, assets, and services all link to.

nodes.label: IP ranges (dhcp/pool/reserved)
nodes.rationale: Named ranges inside a prefix with role dhcp/pool/reserved; shown as bands in the subnet matrix and skipped by allocation.

nodes.label: Subnet matrix (/24-style grid)
nodes.rationale: /24-style grid with one cell per address banded by IP ranges; arrow keys navigate, drag selects a span for bulk actions.

nodes.label: Subnets (prefixes)
nodes.rationale: The heart of the IPAM: each prefix lives inside a VRF, may link to a site and a VLAN, and contains IP addresses — or, as a container, other prefixes.

nodes.label: Tags
nodes.rationale: Colored labels attachable to sites, VRFs, prefixes, and addresses; deleting a tag cleanly drops its assignments everywhere while the tag survives, and vice versa.

nodes.label: VLANs
nodes.rationale: VLANs carry the actual VID (1–4094); prefixes link to a VLAN so the subnet list shows which L2 domain each network rides on.

nodes.label: VRFs
nodes.rationale: Virtual routing & forwarding instances model separate routing tables — the answer to 'the same subnet exists in two places'.

nodes.label: Insecure mode (IPAMBOX_ALLOW_INSECURE)
nodes.rationale: Disables authentication entirely — every request treated as admin; only for use behind a trusted reverse proxy doing its own auth, and it logs a loud startup warning.

nodes.label: Certificate expiry tracking
nodes.rationale: Dashboard surfaces certs_expiring_30d so renewals are visible at login; pairing with a within_days color rule makes urgent renewals unmissable.

nodes.label: IP linking: existing addresses only, never creates
nodes.norm_label: ip linking: existing addresses only, never creates

nodes.label: Match precedence: id → serial_number → mac_address → name+site
nodes.norm_label: match precedence: id → serial_number → mac_address → name+site

nodes.label: NetBox header aliases (device_role→device type, device_type→model, position→U)
nodes.norm_label: netbox header aliases (device_role→device type, device_type→model, position→u)

nodes.label: Scan reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Works both ways: genuinely new hosts require human confirmation, while documented hosts that go quiet flip active→offline→active automatically with no inbox round-trip.

nodes.label: Roll-up utilization
nodes.rationale: agg_used_ips, allocated_pct and descendant_count surface the difference between fully assigned and fully used — a container can be 100% allocated yet 40% used.

nodes.label: import_batch_id provenance
nodes.rationale: Assets arriving through the workbook importer keep import_batch_id provenance back to their upload batch, so imported rows remain traceable to the file that created them.

nodes.label: Key-column merge identity on re-import
nodes.rationale: The key column is the merge identity when the same sheet is re-imported: changed cells update in place, rows absent from the source are kept and reported as 'missing from source' (never silently deleted), and manually edited cells win conflicts — pins, colors, ordering and manual rows always survive.

nodes.label: Positional column keys (c0, c1, …)
nodes.rationale: Columns are keyed positionally so renaming or relabeling a column never touches the stored JSON row data; removing a column only hides it — the cell values are kept.

nodes.label: Color rules
nodes.rationale: Entity/field/operator/value/color rules apply in position order and the first match wins; a manual row color overrides rules for that row (effective tint exposed as display_color); typed fields restrict which operators the editor offers.

nodes.label: Five-stage scan pipeline
nodes.rationale: ARP sweep → ICMP sweep → TCP probe → PTR lookups → OUI resolution; each stage catches hosts silent at the previous layer; persists open_ports and best-effort device_type per host.

nodes.label: Scan targeting policy
nodes.rationale: scan_networks/scan_exclude_networks/scan_only_configured/scan_max_hosts/scan_interface bound what may be scanned; exclusions are enforced identically by the API route, the scheduler, and the worker — a job that slips through one layer is stopped by the next.

nodes.label: Hybrid settings model (.env → database override)
nodes.rationale: .env provides the deployment default; saving in the UI writes an app_settings row that takes effect without a restart; each field shows its source (db/env/default) with a reset button that deletes the override.

nodes.label: Site codes follow site changes flag
nodes.norm_label: site codes follow site changes flag
nodes.rationale: When on (default), linked VRF names and circuit/service site fields update automatically when a site's code, number, or name changes; when off, stored mismatches are treated as deliberate manual overrides.

nodes.label: Next-available IP allocation
nodes.rationale: SELECT … FOR UPDATE plus UNIQUE(vrf_id, address) guarantees concurrent allocations never hand out the same address twice; network/broadcast boundaries and IP ranges are skipped.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL CIDR overlap exclusion
nodes.rationale: Overlapping CIDRs are allowed across VRFs but rejected within a single VRF, enforced by a PostgreSQL exclusion constraint — the database enforces it, not app code or convention.

nodes.label: Device smart file I/O (export dropdown + smart import)
nodes.norm_label: device smart file i/o (export dropdown + smart import)

nodes.label: Excel workbook import (per-sheet detection, dry-run, all-or-nothing/partial commit)
nodes.norm_label: excel workbook import (per-sheet detection, dry-run, all-or-nothing/partial commit)

nodes.label: IPAddress
nodes.rationale: Addresses live inside a prefix and carry both documented intent (status, role, links) and observed reality (scan fields, last seen, mac_mismatch) — the reconciliation unit of the IPAM.

nodes.label: connected_interface_id (structured far-end port link)
nodes.rationale: A structured FK on IPAddress (PATCH /api/v1/addresses/{id}) pointing at the far-end interface the address is patched into. It replaces fragile free text while the legacy switch_name/switch_port columns stay untouched as the import record and display fallback.

nodes.label: connected_ip (host-side NIC binding)
nodes.rationale: Interface field meaning 'this NIC serves this IP' — explicitly a different link from the device's IP ownership and from the address's far-end switch port (connected_interface_id), so the same IP can be viewed from host side and switch side.

nodes.label: DeviceInterface (device-owned port)
nodes.rationale: Interfaces are owned by devices and carry name, kind (rj45/sfp/sfp28/qsfp/console/patch/power/other), speed and MAC — the L1 building block that makes 'what is patched into switch X port 12' a query instead of a memory.

nodes.label: L1 trace (cable path walk)
nodes.rationale: Clicking a cabled port walks the ordered L1 path device-by-device via GET /api/v1/cables/trace?interface_id=. At a patch port the walk continues through the front<->back pair as a 'panel pass-through', so host -> panel-front -> panel-back -> switch renders as one path. Mid-chain launches still surface the whole path; loops terminate at 10 hops.

nodes.label: match-free-text transition endpoint
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/interfaces/match-free-text is a one-shot exact-name matcher: for every address lacking a link, a device whose name exactly equals switch_name AND owns an interface named exactly switch_port gets linked. Multiple candidates are reported 'ambiguous' (never guessed), zero are 'unmatched'; text columns are never touched and every link lands in the changelog for review — a deliberately conservative migration.

nodes.label: One-cable-per-interface rule
nodes.rationale: Each interface terminates at most one cable — mirroring the physical fact that a port holds one plug. Trying to cable a busy port returns the existing cable's id (HTTP 409), so the API fails safe instead of duplicating.

nodes.label: Front/back port pairing (pair partner / pair_interface_id)
nodes.rationale: Each front port is paired to a same-indexed back port (p_i <-> b_i); pairs must live on the same device because they model the two sides of one panel position. The trace treats a pair hop as a 'panel pass-through', not a cable.

nodes.label: Patch Panel (device with patch-kind interfaces)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not a special entity: a patch panel is just a device whose interfaces have kind 'patch', each front port paired to a back port — keeps the object model minimal while still letting the L1 trace pass through the panel.

nodes.label: One-call port generation
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/interfaces/generate creates a whole port set in one call (kind + name prefix + count, optional start_index/speed_mbps); setting pair_prefix additionally creates same-indexed back ports and links each pair — a 24-port patch panel's front+back in one click.

nodes.label: Legacy switch_name/switch_port free text
nodes.rationale: Pre-V4A way of recording the far-end switch port as unstructured text on an address. Kept as the import record and shown as fallback when no structured link exists — never mutated by the transition matcher.

nodes.label: Carrier (shelf/tray slot layout)
nodes.rationale: Real racks hold sub-U gear (half-width switches, RPi trays, quad brackets). A carrier is an ordinary rack device flagged with a slot layout (halves/quarters/shelf); children inherit its U position and face and skip rack-level collision checks because the carrier already reserved that space — single level only.

nodes.label: Device image library (NetBox devicetype-library subset)
nodes.rationale: A bundled ~1,600-entry subset of the NetBox devicetype-library (CC0) served from /rack-library/ inside the app so elevations render real product photos with real dimensions and power/weight — fully air-gapped, refreshed per release by a committed build script.

nodes.label: Rack placement rules
nodes.rationale: Front+rear may legitimately share a U; same-face overlaps are rejected with a conflict; carrier children skip rack-level checks because the carrier already reserved that U and face.

nodes.label: Rack
nodes.rationale: Physical rack elevation: per-U device placement on front/rear faces (front+rear may share a U, same-face overlaps rejected), with health dots, capacity rollups, next-free-U finder, print report and QR labels.

nodes.label: Rack Group (bayed row)
nodes.rationale: A datacenter row is never one rack — groups collect racks standing side by side, render them bottom-aligned like a real bayed row, roll up per-row U/power/weight totals, and allow dragging devices across racks in edit mode.

nodes.label: Rackula round-trip integration
nodes.rationale: Instead of re-implementing a heavy drag-and-drop layout editor, IpamBox round-trips with a self-hosted Rackula instance via share URLs and .Rackula.zip archives; imports preview conflicts and offer merge/replace semantics.

nodes.label: Health rollup: worst status across linked IPs
nodes.norm_label: health rollup: worst status across linked ips

nodes.label: IP address
nodes.rationale: Address rows inside a prefix; record pool membership via ip_range_id; gateway/DNS technical addresses mirrored as protected reserved rows.

nodes.label: IP range (dhcp/pool/reserved)
nodes.rationale: Named ranges inside a prefix shown as bands in the matrix and skipped by allocation; dhcp/pool ranges own their members.

nodes.label: Subnet matrix
nodes.rationale: /24-style utilization grid, one cell per address banded by IP ranges, keyboard navigation, drag-select for bulk actions.

nodes.label: Compose service architecture
nodes.rationale: web (Next.js 15) / api (FastAPI async) / scanner (ARQ worker, host networking, Linux-only) / db (PostgreSQL 16 + btree_gist) / redis (queue+sessions+pub/sub); browser talks only to web via /api/* rewrite; DB and Redis loopback-only.

nodes.label: Backup & restore (.json.gz)
nodes.rationale: Single portable snapshot file; restores are atomic, ID-preserving and schema-checked; users excluded by default and admin accounts never exported so a file can never carry admin credentials.

nodes.label: LAN-Orangutan
nodes.rationale: Cited alongside NetBox as inspiration for the project.

nodes.label: NetBox
nodes.rationale: Cited as inspiration: 'a nod to NetBox ... for proving what good looks like'; also source of the rack image library.

nodes.label: Global row colors
nodes.rationale: Manual per-row colors plus admin-managed field rules; stored in Postgres, computed server-side, covered by backup + changelog.

nodes.label: Gateway & DNS technical rows
nodes.rationale: Prefix gateway (must be inside the prefix) + up to four DNS resolvers; mirrored into protected reserved rows tagged technical:gateway|dns with ⌂/≋ glyphs, excluded from allocation, fully audited.

nodes.label: GiST exclusion constraint (within-VRF overlap)
nodes.rationale: The database enforces overlap rejection, not app code — across VRFs the same CIDR is fine; containers are exempt so they can hold children.

nodes.label: pool_override force
nodes.rationale: Statics inside a dhcp/pool range are rejected because a DHCP server may hand the address to a client; force=1 or a deliberate import records custom_fields.pool_override so overrides stay audited rather than silently allowed.

nodes.label: Prefix (subnet)
nodes.rationale: Heart of the IPAM: lives in a VRF, links a site and VLAN, holds addresses or (as container) child prefixes; statuses active/reserved/deprecated/container.

nodes.label: Atomic next-IP allocation
nodes.rationale: SELECT … FOR UPDATE plus UNIQUE(vrf_id,address) guarantees concurrent allocations never hand out the same address twice.

nodes.label: Changelog audit trail
nodes.rationale: Every create/update/delete recorded with actor, timestamp and field-level before/after diffs; global /changelog page plus per-object history.

nodes.label: GiST overlap exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: Overlapping CIDRs are rejected within a VRF by a PostgreSQL GiST exclusion constraint — the database enforces the rule, not app code, so it cannot be raced or bypassed; container prefixes are exempt so they can hold child subnets.

nodes.label: Site → VRF → Prefix → IP hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Consistency rules are enforced by the database itself, not by convention.

nodes.label: IpamBox
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted, containerized IPAM that keeps the documented network and the real network in sync — drift shows up as data, not surprises.

nodes.label: 4-tier RBAC
nodes.rationale: Administrator / Operator / Contributor / Viewer enforced on every API route, not just hidden in the UI; last admin cannot demote/delete self; role or password change revokes sessions.

nodes.label: Changelog bypass for state writes
nodes.rationale: State columns written via bulk updates that bypass the changelog — steady-state probing produces no audit noise; only target create/edit/delete is audited.

nodes.label: Add network wizard
nodes.rationale: VLAN → subnet → gateway/DNS → DHCP pool → review, created in a single transaction via POST /networks — a half-built network is worse than none.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL GiST CIDR exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: Overlapping CIDRs are allowed across VRFs but rejected within a VRF by a GiST exclusion constraint; container prefixes are exempt so they can hold child subnets.

nodes.label: Event sources
nodes.rationale: One service emits every event: monitor.down/monitor.up (transitions only), cert.expiring (within cert_warn_days, once per cert per day), scan.failed (watchdog/restart failures), mac_mismatch (stored-vs-seen disagreement, once per flag).

nodes.label: Notification channel
nodes.rationale: webhook/discord/telegram/smtp channels; every state transition fans out to ALL enabled channels — per-target routing deliberately out of scope; a broken channel never breaks a check.

nodes.label: Notification log
nodes.rationale: Every delivery attempt recorded — the audit trail for a feature with no alert acknowledgement; retention via notify_retention_days (0 = keep).

nodes.label: Settings → Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Admin surface: channel CRUD + test button (exercises the real secret end-to-end), runtime toggles (monitoring_enabled, monitor_concurrency, monitor_http_timeout, notify_retention_days) and the log viewer.

nodes.label: Certificate expiry tracking
nodes.rationale: Extended entity with a 30-day expiry countdown; source of cert.expiring notification events.

nodes.label: Notification channels (webhook/SMTP/Discord/Telegram)
nodes.rationale: Carry monitor transitions plus cert.expiring, scan.failed and mac_mismatch events; every delivery attempt recorded in the notification log.

nodes.label: Check kinds (ping/tcp/http)
nodes.rationale: ping = ICMP echo; tcp = connect on port; http = GET http://{ip}:{port}{http_path} matched against http_expect (empty = any 2xx/3xx, status:NNN = exact code, else case-sensitive body substring); plain HTTP only, no TLS validation.

nodes.label: down_after hysteresis
nodes.rationale: A target flips down only after down_after consecutive failures so one dropped packet won't page anyone; recovery fires on first success — no flapping alerts, and steady-state probe writes bypass the changelog to avoid audit noise.

nodes.label: Monitor target
nodes.rationale: Anchors to exactly one device (probes first active IP, falling back to lowest-id address so renumbering doesn't break it) or one IP address; deleting the anchor deletes its monitors.

nodes.label: Secrets-at-rest contract
nodes.rationale: Channel secrets are AES-256-GCM encrypted under IPAMBOX_SECRET_KEY and write-only in the API because webhook URLs carry tokens in their path; without a configured master key, channel create/test returns 503.

nodes.label: Discovery Inbox reconciliation
nodes.rationale: New hosts land as discovered (bulk confirm/delete), missing active hosts go offline, returning hosts flip back to active; stored-vs-seen MAC disagreement flags mac_mismatch for review.

nodes.label: Health monitoring & notification channels
nodes.rationale: Per-target ping/tcp/http health checks anchored to a device or IP address; answers 'is it alive right now' versus the scanner's sweeps.

nodes.label: LAN scanner (ARP/ICMP/TCP)
nodes.rationale: ARP sweep → ICMP ping-socket → TCP port probe → PTR lookups → IEEE OUI vendor resolution; persists open_ports and best-effort device_type; scheduled via SCAN_INTERVAL_MINUTES; cancellable jobs with SSE live progress.

nodes.label: Deliberate limits
nodes.rationale: By design: no SNMP monitors, no dependency/rollup trees, no maintenance windows, no alert acknowledgement, no per-target routing, no uptime-percentage history — the notification log is the audit trail.

nodes.label: Monitor state machine & hysteresis
nodes.rationale: state (unknown→up/down) plus consecutive_failures: down fires only at down_after (default 2) so one dropped packet won't page anyone; up fires on first success; unknown→up silent, unknown→down alerts.

nodes.label: Batched sweep tick
nodes.rationale: Per-minute worker tick picks targets whose interval_seconds elapsed (cap 200/tick) and runs them in ONE batched sweep job sharing the max_jobs pool — monitoring never starves scans.

nodes.label: down_after hysteresis
nodes.rationale: A target flips down only after down_after consecutive failures and recovers on the first success — no flapping alerts; steady state stays silent and never touches the changelog.

nodes.label: Batched monitor sweep lane
nodes.rationale: A per-minute cron batches all due targets into ONE run_monitor_sweep job with semaphore-bounded probes, so monitoring shares the max_jobs=4 pool without starving scans.

nodes.label: Encrypted channel secrets
nodes.rationale: Channel secrets (webhook URLs, SMTP passwords, bot tokens) are encrypted with IPAMBOX_SECRET_KEY and are write-only in the API.

nodes.label: Accounts & role-based access control
nodes.rationale: RBAC enforced on every API route — the UI only hides what you can't do; the backend is the authority.

nodes.label: Expiry tracking (badge, certs_expiring_30d dashboard count)
nodes.rationale: Dashboard surfaces certificates expiring within 30 days so renewals are visible the moment you log in.

nodes.label: Certificates — expiry tracking register
nodes.rationale: Track certificate expiry across the estate so nothing silently lapses.

nodes.label: Circuits — WAN circuit register
nodes.rationale: One row per provider line, linked to a site.

nodes.label: Circuit fields (line type, Bezeq circuit ID, WAN IP, is_retired)
nodes.norm_label: circuit fields (line type, bezeq circuit id, wan ip, is_retired)
nodes.rationale: is_retired keeps history without deleting; site_number/site_code/site_name denormalized for fast lists.

nodes.label: Discovery Inbox — reconciliation queue
nodes.rationale: Scan findings land in an inbox instead of silently mutating documented data.

nodes.label: Hierarchy tree (/tree) — Site→VRF→Prefix
nodes.rationale: Fastest way to see where a subnet lives and how full each branch is.

nodes.label: Data model — Site→VRF→Prefix→IP address
nodes.rationale: Everything hangs off one hierarchy; VLANs, IP ranges, tags and row colors sit around the core.

nodes.label: Overview — what IpamBox is
nodes.rationale: Documented network vs real network kept in sync; drift shows up as data instead of surprises.

nodes.label: Manual row colors (per-row Set color)
nodes.rationale: Every list has a Set color action; a legend button explains the tints currently in use.

nodes.label: Color rules — admin-managed conditional row coloring
nodes.norm_label: color rules — admin-managed conditional row coloring
nodes.rationale: Rules apply in position order and the first matching rule wins; a manual row color overrides rules, exposed as display_color. Operators: eq, neq, contains, lt, gt, within_days.

nodes.label: Scans — Scapy raw-socket LAN scanner
nodes.rationale: Runs with network_mode: host plus NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW for real L2 access — Linux only.

nodes.label: Command palette (⌘K/Ctrl+K)
nodes.rationale: Searches the whole IPAM including matching Docs guides; pasting a bare IP offers a Jump result landing on the owning prefix — preferring the documented owner, then the deepest containing prefix. Hebrew final-letter folding supported.

nodes.label: Services as blast-radius mapping
nodes.rationale: When a subnet changes or a scan finds drift the question is 'who cares?' — linking services to sites makes the circuits, certificates and assets of that site one hop away.

nodes.label: Services — service catalog
nodes.rationale: What the network serves, not just what it's made of.

nodes.label: Service fields (beneficiary, site, doc path, test info)
nodes.norm_label: service fields (beneficiary, site, doc path, test info)

nodes.label: Site-cascade feature flag (codes follow site changes)
nodes.norm_label: site-cascade feature flag (codes follow site changes)
nodes.rationale: When on, linked VRF names and circuit/service site fields update automatically on site code/number/name changes; when off, stored mismatches are treated as deliberate manual overrides.

nodes.label: Sites — top of the IpamBox hierarchy
nodes.norm_label: sites — top of the ipambox hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Physical or logical locations; VRFs, VLANs, prefixes, circuits, assets and services all link to a site.

nodes.label: VLAN fields (VID 1–4094, name, group, site, status)
nodes.norm_label: vlan fields (vid 1–4094, name, group, site, status)

nodes.label: VRFs — virtual routing & forwarding instances
nodes.rationale: The answer to 'the same subnet exists in two places' — model separate routing tables.

nodes.norm_label: vrf fields (name, rd, site) + seeded global vrf
nodes.rationale: A Global VRF is seeded by the initial migration so a fresh install always has somewhere to put prefixes.

nodes.label: Demo CSV files
nodes.rationale: demo-site-utf8/cp1255 (encoding fallback), demo-addresses.csv (bulk address import), demo-contacts-list/demo-vlans/demo-servers-list (custom lists exercising every inferred column type).

nodes.label: Demo VLAN scheme
nodes.rationale: Stable subnet↔VLAN enterprise plan across both workbooks and demo-vlans.csv; commit auto-creates VLAN records scoped per site; groups are manual.

nodes.label: Network_Address_DEMO.xlsx
nodes.rationale: Clean flagship 63-sheet Hebrew+English workbook; designed to import perfectly (all creates, zero conflicts) while exercising every sheet family.

nodes.label: Network_Address_DEMO_EN.xlsx
nodes.rationale: Compact 44-sheet English workbook that is deliberately messy — headerless sheets, blank IP headers, duplicated column blocks, orphan ranges, empty sheets — each maps to a code path in backend/app/services/workbook/.

nodes.label: Stats strip & saved views
nodes.rationale: Click-to-filter stat cards (EOL passed, EOL<90d, missing serial, no site) plus built-in saved views.

nodes.label: Live IP column resolution
nodes.rationale: ip columns resolve live against ip_addresses (status dot, last-seen, click → drawer); unresolved IPs render muted/dashed, surfacing drift between the list and the IPAM.

nodes.label: Hebrew data support
nodes.rationale: Final-letter folding in search, dir=auto on free-text cells, LTR-pinned IP/MAC columns, Hebrew-safe site slugs.

nodes.label: Excel workbook import
nodes.rationale: Network_Address.xlsx-style import: per-sheet type detection, dry-run preview with per-row conflict report, all-or-nothing or partial commit; handles split-octet IPs, multi-IP cells, four MAC formats, Excel serial dates, repeated headers, duplicated column blocks; Hebrew normalized; per-row provenance to upload batch.

nodes.label: Asset (HW/SW inventory with serials)
nodes.rationale: Hardware/software register with kind, category, vendor/model, EOL date, support status, serial number (primary tracking key) and site.

nodes.label: Typed list columns (text/ip/date/select/number/url/owner)
nodes.rationale: text/ip/date/select/number/url/owner column types with per-type rendering: select chips, expiry badges, clickable URLs, live IP resolution.

nodes.label: Custom list
nodes.rationale: User-defined typed tables for sheet-shaped data that doesn't fit a fixed entity — keeps 'שרתים בייצור' a table with a Guest OS column instead of dissolving into asset notes.

nodes.label: Key column merge identity
nodes.rationale: Columns are keyed positionally (c0, c1…) so renaming never touches stored data; the key column is the merge identity on re-import — manual edits win conflicts, absent rows are kept and reported 'missing from source', never silently deleted.

nodes.label: Fictional demo dataset
nodes.rationale: All values invented — the files mirror the shape of a real Network_Address.xlsx so the import pipeline can be exercised end-to-end with zero production data.

nodes.label: import_batch_id provenance
nodes.rationale: Imported assets keep import_batch_id provenance back to their upload batch.

nodes.label: Positional column keys (c0, c1, …)
nodes.rationale: Columns are keyed positionally so renaming or relabeling never touches stored data; removing a column hides it while cell values are kept.
